title: Cyber Defenders Unit 5 · Kind screens, safe chats (6-8)

items.q: What may an online-only friend safely know about you?
choices: Your live location, switched on all day
Your school and daily route
Less than a real-life friend: a nickname and your game talk
Everything a real-life friend knows
items.why: An online-only friend can be real company, but they get less than a real-life friend: no live location, school or route.

items.q: You want to post a great photo that includes two friends. What does consent require?
choices: Post first; they can complain later
A yes from the person who took it only
A clear yes from everyone in the photo
No yes if the photo is flattering
items.why: Everyone in the photo gets their own yes, before it is posted. Who took it, or how good it looks, does not replace that.

items.q: In a group chat, a friend dares you to share your live location to prove trust. What is happening?
choices: A normal friendship test
Pressure, and leaving or refusing is a complete answer
A safety feature of the chat
A dare you must accept to stay in the group
items.why: Sharing your live location to prove trust is pressure, not friendship. Saying no, or leaving, is a complete answer.

items.q: Two friends fall out in a group chat and both give as good as they get. A classmate is mocked daily by a group and cannot make it stop. Which is cyberbullying?
choices: The fall-out, because it is louder
Neither; both are jokes
Both equally
The daily mocking: a pattern with a power gap
items.why: A two-sided fall-out is a conflict. Cyberbullying is a pattern aimed at one person who cannot make it stop: a power gap.

items.q: You are a bystander while a classmate is targeted in a chat. Which move does the most good?
choices: Save the evidence, report it, and back the target
Debate the actor for an hour
Forward the thread to another school
Watch silently so you stay safe and neutral
items.why: Saving, reporting and backing the target change things. Arguing, spreading it or staying silent leave the target alone.

items.q: A post attacks a student for who they are. What is the Defender response to hate speech?
choices: Debate it point by point
Ignore it completely
Report it, save it, and support the person targeted
Quote it to show friends
items.why: Debating or quoting hate speech spreads it, and ignoring it leaves the target alone. Report it, save it and support them.

items.q: A video ends and the next one starts by itself while a red badge counts your unread alerts. Which hooks are at work?
choices: Autoplay and notifications
Backups and updates
Passphrases and padlocks
Ciphers and checksums
items.why: Neither one waits for you to choose: the next video starts on its own and the badge pulls you back. Apps add them to keep you watching longer.

items.q: Which setting change answers an endless-scroll feed?
choices: A brighter screen
A time limit you chose, with autoplay off
A longer passphrase
More notifications
items.why: An endless feed has no natural stopping point. A time limit you chose, with autoplay off, gives it one.

items.q: Why is just try harder the wrong frame for screen balance?
choices: Willpower is illegal in apps
Trying harder always works instantly
The app is engineered to hold attention, so fix the design and settings
Balance does not matter at all
items.why: Apps are designed to hold attention, so willpower alone is an unfair fight. Change the settings and the design instead.
